stem:
Lalit measures a ribbon as $45$ millimetres long. He needs the length in centimetres. There are $10$ millimetres in $1$ centimetre.

Which conversion is correct?

options.text: Report the answer as "centimetre", naming the unit instead of writing the decimal length.
Say that centimetres are what produce millimetres, so he must invent $45$ mm from a finished centimetre reading.
$45$ mm $= 4.5$ cm, because each millimetre is $0.1$ of a centimetre.
Write $45$ cm, copying the printed digits $45$ without shifting by the $10$-to-$1$ place relation.

teacher.key_rationale: When 10 smaller units make 1 larger unit, each smaller unit is 0.1 of the larger: 45 mm = 4.5 cm. Naming the unit, reversing the conversion, or copying 45 without the place shift all miss the decimal link.
